tutorial.title: Sandbox tasks
tutorial.hint: Complete this step to unlock the next one.
tutorial.catalogueDescription: Create a new product, such as a hoodie in different sizes and colours. Enter a price and select ‘Save configuration’. In the variants below, choose how the product should be offered. You can also use minimum and target stock to decide how many items you want to keep in stock and when a warning should appear.
tutorial.purchaseDescription: Refill your stock: select a product and variant, enter the purchase price and quantity, and add any other useful details. Then book the purchase.
tutorial.saleDescription: The gig is over and the merch stand is busy: add a few products to the basket, choose the payment method and confirm the sale. Try shipping a product too – you will find it afterwards under ‘Open tasks’.
tutorial.balanceDescription: How much did you take and which stock needs refilling? Find out in the Balances tab. If you entered target stock for products, Purchases can also create a shopping list for you automatically.
tutorial.optionalHint: You have completed the introduction. These steps are optional and can be tried in any order.
tutorial.shipping: Book a shipment and edit the open task
tutorial.shippingDescription: Add products to the basket in Sales and choose ‘Book as shipment’. Then open ‘Open tasks’ to edit shipping costs, shipment status or other details and complete the task.
tutorial.cancellationDescription: Open History and expand the sale receipt you want to change. You can cancel the entire sale or individual items; stock and balances are corrected accordingly.
tutorial.slideshowDescription: Open the slideshow, select the product images you want and start the presentation for your merch stand. You can leave the full-screen view at any time.
tutorial.packingDescription: Open the packing list, create a container or gig bag and add the products you want to take. While packing, you can mark their status directly in the list.
tutorial.rolesDescription: Use the yellow sandbox banner at the top to switch between seller, member, manager and band admin. This shows which views and actions are available to each role.
tutorial.locked: Complete the current sandbox task first or choose ‘Skip’.

telemetryConsent.title: Pseudonymised usage statistics
telemetryConsent.intro: Help us understand which features are actually useful and where Merch Manager should improve.
telemetryConsent.anonymousTitle: No real names or IP addresses
telemetryConsent.anonymousText: Operations receive stable, opaque aliases for the band, article and operation. This allows several operations from the same band or article to be compared without storing their original names or IDs. Collected data may include feature usage, data volumes, storage usage, roles, payment method, quantity and price, open/completed status and the event/location text entered by the band. Band/user names, internal user/band/article IDs, IP addresses, customer names/addresses, contact details and comments are not stored.
telemetryConsent.collects: The data helps us find rarely used features, understand performance and data volumes, and prioritise development. Telemetry data is not shared with third parties.
telemetryConsent.allowHint: Collection for your account starts only after you save this choice.
telemetryConsent.denyHint: No telemetry is collected for this account.
telemetryConsent.later: You can change this setting at any time in your account.

telemetryAdmin.title: Statistics
telemetryAdmin.intro: Summary and pseudonymised operations from accounts that opted in.
telemetryAdmin.privacy: Detailed rows use stable pseudonyms for band, article and operation. Real names, internal IDs, IP addresses, customer/contact data and comments are not stored. Telemetry data is not shared with third parties.
telemetryAdmin.locationHint: Only the event/location text selected by the band; no IP geolocation.
telemetryAdmin.recentHint: The latest observed state is shown per operation. The complete event history is available in the JSON download.

users.roleHelpIntro: Which role is right for whom?

roleDescriptions.seller: Sellers are the people helping out at your merch stand. They can ring up sales, but they cannot access your administration, purchasing, or finance areas.
roleDescriptions.member: Members are part of your band. In addition to selling, they can view the shared band areas and ongoing tasks, but they cannot manage products, finances, or user accounts.
roleDescriptions.manager: Managers handle the day-to-day merch operation. They can manage products, purchases, band finances, and the product showcase, but they cannot manage users or approve support access.
roleDescriptions.band_admin: Band admins have full control of the band's workspace. On top of all manager permissions, they manage users and roles, payment details, and support-access requests.

hero.title: Sell merch. Know your stock. Keep clean books.
hero.lead: Say goodbye to scattered notes, clunky band tools, and messy spreadsheets. Merch Manager keeps your sales, inventory, and band finances in one place — free, browser-based, and available offline.
hero.mobile: Optimized for pc, phones and tablets

interactive.kicker: One tool for the whole tour
interactive.title: From packing to accounting.
interactive.lead: Discover how Merch Manager connects your workflows around touring, the merch booth and band finances.
interactive.sceneDescription: A panoramic illustration showing analytics, a packing list, a merchandise booth and a concert stage. Six areas are interactive.
interactive.instructions: Use Tab to choose a feature area. Enter or Space keeps it active.

A.title: Bestsellers & band finances
A.description: Which shirt sells best? How much profit did the last gig make? Keep an eye on your band's finances.

B.title: Packing list

C.title: Book sales anywhere
C.description: Record all your sales – whether you're using a smartphone, tablet or PC.

purpose.question: What do I need Merch Manager for?
purpose.answer: It keeps your band's sales, stock, purchases, packing lists and shared expenses in one place. You can immediately see what sold, what needs restocking and how your merchandise and band finances are doing.

deletion.question: Why can't I delete some transactions and variants?
deletion.answer: Trust is good, control is better: booked transactions remain available for a traceable history and can be cancelled instead. Saved variant options remain in place so stock and earlier bookings are not accidentally assigned to a new variant. Unsaved input can still be discarded.

costs.question: Does it cost anything?
costs.answer: No. There are currently no plans to charge for using it in the future either.

shopApi.question: Will there be an integration with online shops?
shopApi.answer: An integration with shop APIs is not currently planned. Merch Manager focuses on direct sales, stock and your band's workflows.

sandbox.question: Can I try everything without signing up?
sandbox.answer: Yes. The full sandbox uses isolated demo data and cannot affect a real band. It is deleted automatically after it expires.

offline.question: Does Merch Manager work without internet access?
offline.answer: Sales and packing lists remain usable offline after the first load. New operations are queued locally and synchronised when the connection returns.

landing.footer: Sales, inventory and band finances in one shared tool.

telemetry.title: Pseudonymised usage statistics
telemetry.intro: This choice applies only to your account and is independent of other members of your band.
telemetry.anonymousText: Feature and operation data may be stored with stable, opaque aliases for band, article and operation. This includes data volumes, storage usage, roles, payment method, quantity/price, status and the entered event/location text. Real names, internal user/band/article IDs, IP addresses, customer/contact data and comments are not stored. The data is not shared with third parties.
telemetry.stopHint: Turning this off stops all future telemetry for your account. Previously stored pseudonymised operations contain no user ID.
